name: Kamara
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress
sweep_summary: Kamara (kama1357) is not in the catalog and this search of works with stress in the title turned up a single stress-titled item, Hunt 1988 'Tone and stress analysis by computer' (Notes on Linguistics 41: 14-18), which was already held by the project from the hang1258 search (archive.org scan of the NOL 41-43 issue run, ERIC ED340197) and was read in full. It is a hardware/software note on an acoustic F0/amplitude analyzer tested on Hanga utterances (plus Nambiquara, Cantonese, Minyanka, Arabic, Tamil); it never mentions Kamara (0 hits in the whole issue-run scanned) and states no rule of word-stress placement even for Hanga -- only that one low-toned Hanga syllable was 'the most stressed syllable in the utterance' (p.16). Glottolog's link to kama1357 comes from Maho's Africa bibliography, which treats Kamara as a Hanga co-dialect. So: no first-hand statement of Kamara word stress exists in this search of works with stress in the title (no new stress statement was found). The only accent remark for Kamara held by the project remains the ethnonym note in Naden 1999 (Gur Papers 4: 75, 'Ka'mara/Ka'marsi with very weak initial syllable and strongly accented second'), already logged in the 9/16; Naden 2015 dictionary and Naden 2021/2024 comparative dictionaries have no prosody. Not obtainable online and still the likeliest place for a Kamara phonology statement: Prost 1974, Notes sur le Kamara de Bouna, Annales de l'Universite d'Abidjan Serie H VII(1): 75-94 (print only; Glottolog Glottolog's most extensive description). txt) and a line appended to there. Glottolog reference 54334 and the archive.org item page were downloaded directly to verify the record.

sources.citation: Naden, Tony. 1999. Notes on the Kamara of Larabanga. Gur Papers / Cahiers Voltaïques 4: 75-89. (author's 17-page scan posted on his Aardvarks Lexico site; scanned with tesseract)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: §1.1 'Phonetics and phonology' (p.76) covers only long vowels, surface CVCV with transition ('weak') vowels, and the [ɣ] allophone of /g/; no word-stress or tone rule. The only accent remark in the paper is about the ethnonym: 'The Kamara (Ka'mara/Ka'marsi with very weak initial syllable and strongly accented second)' (§0.1, p.75). States Kamara is 'probably mutually-intelligible with the better-known Hanga.. functionally a co-dialect' and refers to Hunt/Hunt 1981 for Hanga phonology.
